title: Near- and Medium-term Outlook for Inflation in Singapore and Steps to Mitigate Sharp Rise
what_it_is: Near- and Medium-term Outlook for Inflation in Singapore and Steps to Mitigate Sharp Rise

sections.label: CPI-All Items inflation Q3 2021
sections.summary: CPI-All Items inflation rose to 2.5% year-on-year in Q3 2021, up from 2.3% in Q2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: CPI-All Items inflation picked up to 2.5% on a year-on-year basis in Q32021, from 2.3% in Q2.

sections.label: CPI inflation projections
sections.summary: CPI-All Items inflation is projected at around 2% this year and 1.5% to 2.5% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, CPI-All Items inflation is projected to come in at around 2% this year and average 1.5% to 2.5% in 2022.

sections.label: MAS Singapore dollar appreciating path
sections.summary: MAS announced a shift towards an appreciating path for the trade-weighted Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: First, in view of the external and domestic cost pressures, MAS recently announced a shift towards an appreciating path for the trade-weighted Singapore dollar – the Singapore dollar nominal effective exchange rate.

sections.label: Retail Price Watch Group measures
sections.summary: The Retail Price Watch Group stood down, but other measures monitor goods prices, with Government working with cooperatives and community programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Retail Price Watch Group that the Member mentioned has stood down but we have other measures and ways of monitoring the price of goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: To also help Singaporeans cope with higher prices for their daily necessities, the Government continues to work with cooperatives, such as NTUC FairPrice and community support programmes, such as the price freezes on essential items under house brands over the period of March 2019 to December 2020.

sections.label: Diversifying food and energy sources
sections.summary: Food and energy import sources are being diversified long term, with assistance to lower-income households including U-Save vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Third, is diversifying food import sources and energy sources over the long term, as we have debated in the House for the last two days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And of course, our particular focus and assistance to lower-income households, including, for example, U-Save vouchers for households living in for 4-room or smaller HDB flats to help them with utility bills.

sections.label: US consumer price inflation
sections.summary: US consumer price inflation is at 5.4%, the highest in 13 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: If you look at it, US consumer price inflation is at 5.4%, the highest in 13 years.

sections.label: Non-oil domestic exports growth
sections.summary: NODX rose 9.1% year-on-year in Q3 2021, after a 10.1% expansion in Q2 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Our non-oil domestic exports (NODX) increased 9.1% year-on-year in Q3 2021, following the 10.1% expansion in Q2 2021.

sections.label: Trade facilitation and multilateral frameworks
sections.summary: Major trade facilitation and multilateral frameworks like RCEP and CPTPP build on existing FTAs covering 85% of global GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The Member knows that we have undertaken a whole slew and suite of major trade facilitation and multilateral frameworks, such as RCEP, CPTPP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: These build upon our existing FTAs with major trade partners, representing 85% of global GDP.
